summary.title: Defensive Programming & Resilient systems in Real World (TM)
summary.one_liner: Practical resilience techniques for production systems: isolate failures, use timeouts and circuit breakers, feature-flag risky changes, and log with purpose.
takeaways: Bugs can't be eliminated, so systems must be designed to survive them and contain their effects.
Set timeouts on every integration point and consider failing fast to prevent cascading failures.
Use circuit breakers, limit and log retries, and check whether a prior operation is still pending before retrying state-changing calls.
Reduce release risk with dark launches, feature disabling, hot-reloadable configuration, and keeping old code until new code is proven.
Reserve ERROR logs for serious problems, rotate logs, and use logging and monitoring to understand normal system behavior.
summary.summary: This is a slide deck from Tuenti on building resilient software for production. It argues that bugs will happen and must be survived, that resilience comes from replication, containment, isolation and delegation, and that design choices carry financial cost. Practical guidance covers isolating subsystems, health checks, timeouts, fail-fast behavior, circuit breakers, bounded retries, and careful handling of state-changing operations. It also covers safe deployment via dark launches, feature disabling, and hot-reloaded configuration, plus logging and monitoring practices. The page is terse slide text, so the points are summarized as bullet-style notes rather than detailed explanations.
